bindings.label: Patient presented with sudden loss of consciousness and foaming at the mouth

Patient is in their 60s; complained of chest discomfort for the past 1 month and was taking Chinese medicine; drank about 180 mL of Chinese herbal medicine 20 minutes before developing syncope; vomit had a pale yellow color
Patient had no history of arrhythmias and no family history of sudden unexpected death or fatal cerebrovascular accident

Physical examination showed temperature 36°C, heart rate 124 beats/min, blood pressure 55/32 mm Hg, pulse oximetry 99% on room air, pupils 3 mm in diameter and reactive to light, skin cool moist and cyanosed, lung fields clear, and heart sounds indistinguishable due to tachycardia
ECG shows wide QRS tachycardia with alternating axis and AV dissociation (bidirectional ventricular tachycardia)
Follow-up ECG shows Q waves and T wave inversion indicating myocardial injury
Aconitine-induced cardiotoxicity (herbal medicine poisoning) is the cause of the patient's cardiovascular collapse
Aconitine-induced cardiotoxicity has caused secondary myocardial injury
